note: Original factual annotations. Event URLs cite dates and claims; coordinates locate the named place approximately, not battlefield boundaries. BC dates use astronomical years (1 BC = 0).

items.title: Rome’s monuments
items.text: Forums, the Pantheon and imperial monuments remain embedded in Rome’s later city.

items.title: Pont du Gard
items.text: The aqueduct bridge preserves Roman hydraulic construction; UNESCO’s detailed statement dates the aqueduct to the middle of the first century.
items.source: UNESCO, Pont du Gard: Outstanding Universal Value

items.title: Hadrian’s Wall survives
items.text: Surviving wall, forts and civilian settlements make the frontier visible as archaeology.
items.source: UNESCO, Frontiers of the Roman Empire

items.title: Ravenna’s mosaics
items.text: Ravenna’s monuments preserve late Roman and Byzantine religious and artistic history.
items.source: UNESCO, Early Christian Monuments of Ravenna

items.title: Constantinople’s inheritance
items.text: The eastern Roman tradition forms part of Istanbul’s layered history; the city is not reduced to one ancient identity.
